turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his actions had consequences, and that if he continued to oppress Nikhil's tenantry, he would not hesitate to take measures to protect them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and told Nikhil that it seemed his own tenantry was afraid of Nikhil's authority, and that he should be grateful that his estate was so well-liked.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that his own tenantry's loyalty was not in question, but that Sandip's actions were causing them undue hardship, and that he would not stand idly by while they suffered.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was wasting his breath with such empty threats, and that the real fear was not of the Mussulmans, but of being outdone by his own ineptitude.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil informed Sandip that his estate was not as secure as he thought, and that the tensions with the Mussulmans were not to be taken lightly.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he believed the tensions with the Mussulmans were truly so dire, and what measures he thought would be necessary to mitigate them.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned that the growing tensions with the Mussulmans would soon boil over into violence, and that Sandip's estate would not be spared.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip scoffed at Nikhil's dire warnings, calling them the ramblings of a nervous old man.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip take immediate action to secure his estate, lest he suffer the consequences of his own complacency.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if he truly believed the tensions with the Mussulmans were just a matter of idle gossip, or if he had heard something that had led him to be so dismissive of Nikhil's warnings.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and told Nikhil that he was more concerned about the state of Nikhil's own estate, which seemed to be crumbling faster than the relationships between the Mussulmans and themselves.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil asked Sandip how he could so callously dismiss the very real threats posed by the growing tensions between Hindus and Mussulmans, when the safety and security of his own family and estate were at stake.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his warnings were as dramatic as the plot twists in a cheap novel, and that he would not be swayed by such theatrics.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his careless attitude would only serve to embolden the Mussulmans, and that the consequences of his actions would be borne not just by himself, but by his family and community as well.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip smirked and asked Nikhil if he had ever considered the possibility that the real threat to their estates was not the Mussulmans, but Nikhil's own ineptitude at managing his lands.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his jocular remarks were a poor substitute for meaningful action, and that he expected a more responsible response from a fellow zamindar.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted in derision, telling Nikhil that he was more concerned with salvaging his own reputation than with the actual well-being of the people on his lands.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that the well-being of his people was of the utmost importance and that he would not be swayed by petty squabbles or personal animosities.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Bimala, as she stood quietly observing the exchange, if she had not found Nikhil's solemn warnings to be as thrilling as a bad poem.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the root causes of the tensions between the zamindars and the local Mussulmans, rather than merely warning them of potential attacks.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
